result.target_topic: Product Demand and Margin Volatility Risks
result.target_summary: Product demand varies by market segment and is difficult to forecast due to macroeconomic conditions, consumer confidence, and technology trends; shifts from higher-margin to lower-margin products, such as the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors produced at external foundries, have decreased and may continue to decrease gross margin percentages.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures address the risks associated with changes in product demand across market segments, the difficulty in forecasting demand, and the potential impact on revenue and gross margins due to shifts in product mix (e.g., higher-end to lower-margin).

previous_disclosures.section: Consolidated Results of Operations > Risk Factors and Other Key Information > Risk Factors
previous_disclosures.summary: Changes in product demand across segments like PC, CCG, DCAI, and NEX, influenced by macroeconomic conditions, geopolitical tensions, and competitive pressures, can reduce revenue, lower gross margins, or require asset write-downs, with pricing variability further impacting profitability.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosure focuses on the risk that product demand is difficult to forecast and that shifts from higher-margin to lower-margin products (specifically citing Intel Core Ultra 200V processors produced at external foundries) decrease gross margin. The 2025 search results show product performance disclosures (e.g., intc_2025_7_D024, intc_2025_7_D028) but do not contain a risk factor specifically highlighting the margin impact of shifting to lower-margin products like the Core Ultra 200V or similar external-foundry products as a key risk. intc_2025_7_D015 mentions Core Ultra Series 3 on Intel 18A, but not the margin risk context. Therefore, no direct counterpart addressing this specific margin/product mix risk was found.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure specifically identifies a margin erosion risk caused by a product mix shift towards lower-margin external foundry products (Core Ultra 200V). The removal of this specific product-level margin risk analysis in 2025 changes the disclosure regarding the profitability impact of Intel's manufacturing strategy changes. It is a specific financial operational risk that is no longer explicitly highlighted in the same manner.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Removal of product mix margin erosion risks

comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue increased to 49% in 2024 from 46% in 2023. This increase was primarily driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues, as well as lower Gaming revenue, which was partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss how shifts in revenue mix and product types impact gross margin. Intel explicitly states that shifts from higher-margin products to lower-margin products (like externally manufactured Core Ultra 200V) have decreased its gross margin. In contrast, AMD reports that a favorable shift in revenue mix toward higher Data Center and Client revenues drove its gross margin increase to 49% in 2024.

sentences.text: To the extent demand shifts from our higher-margin to lower-margin products in any of our market segments, as has been the case with the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors, our gross margin percentage has decreased and may decrease again.

Some of our higher-priced products, however, such as the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors launched in September 2024, have lower margins as they are produced at external foundries rather than in our manufacturing facilities.
Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue was 49% in 2024 compared to 46% in 2023.
The increase in gross margin was due to a favorable shift in revenue mix of higher Data Center and Client revenues, lower Gaming revenue, partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.

comparisons.peer_topic: Gross margin financial results and VMware impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin increased to $32,509 million in fiscal year 2024 from $24,690 million in fiscal year 2023, primarily due to VMware contributions offset by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets. As a percentage of net revenue, gross margin decreased to 63% from 69%, driven by the same amortization factors, less favorable semiconductor product mix, and offsets from infrastructure software margins.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies attribute changes in gross margin percentages to product mix factors. Intel notes that gross margin decreased due to demand shifts to lower-margin products like the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors. Broadcom reports that its gross margin percentage decreased to 63% from 69%, driven by less favorable margin within the semiconductor solutions segment specifically due to product mix, despite total gross margin dollars increasing due to VMware.

sentences.text: To the extent demand shifts from our higher-margin to lower-margin products in any of our market segments, as has been the case with the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors, our gross margin percentage has decreased and may decrease again.

Some of our higher-priced products, however, such as the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors launched in September 2024, have lower margins as they are produced at external foundries rather than in our manufacturing facilities.
The decrease was primarily due to higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger.
In addition, gross margin contributions from our infrastructure software segment were partially offset by less favorable margin within the semiconductor solutions segment driven by product mix.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the impact of product demand and market conditions on margins, including inventory-related impacts. Intel warns that changes in demand may reduce revenue and gross margin or require asset write-downs. Micron details how its gross margin improved to 22% in 2024, partly due to lower costs from selling inventories that had been written down in the previous year, highlighting the direct link between demand assumptions, inventory values, and margin outcomes.

sentences.text: Changes in the demand for our products have in the past and may in the future reduce our revenue, lower our gross margin, or require us to write down the value of our assets.

Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).

comparisons.peer_topic: Fiscal 2024 gross margin performance and drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023, primarily driven by 217% growth in Data Center revenue and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss gross margin performance and the drivers behind it, though the specific drivers differ. Intel cites shifts to lower-margin external foundry products as a headwind to gross margin. NVIDIA cites strong Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as primary drivers for its significant gross margin increase to 72.7% in fiscal 2024.

sentences.text: To the extent demand shifts from our higher-margin to lower-margin products in any of our market segments, as has been the case with the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors, our gross margin percentage has decreased and may decrease again.

Some of our higher-priced products, however, such as the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors launched in September 2024, have lower margins as they are produced at external foundries rather than in our manufacturing facilities.
Our overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023.
The year over year increase was primarily due to strong Data Center revenue growth of 217% and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
